title: Playwright vs. Puppeteer: Head-to-head Comparison 2026
partialText: Playwright and Puppeteer are top browser automation tools, but they serve different needs. Playwright excels in cross-browser support, scalability, and reliability with features like auto-waiting and BrowserContexts. Puppeteer is faster and simpler for Chromium-focused tasks. For large-scale scraping, combining either tool with proxies is essential to avoid blocks and ensure consistent performance.

title: How AI Agents Are Reshaping Software Delivery in 2026
partialText: AI is no longer just helping developers write code. In 2026, AI agents are starting to influence the full software delivery lifecycle. The biggest change is not that AI writes more code, but that it reduces friction between planning, execution, testing, and release.

title: In the AI Era, Saving Time Is the Ultimate Life Hack
partialText: AI is helping people save time, reduce friction, and work smarter in everyday life.

title: When AI Agents Fail, Who Owns the Fallout?
partialText: In the world of security and DevOps, AI agents are being pushed from demos into production quickly. When an AI agent fails, it can be hard to tell who made the call, why it happened, or what evidence exists to explain it. This is even more difficult in multi-agent systems, where responsibility is distributed across models, tools, orchestrators, and human operators.

title: Educational Byte: What Is a Trojan and How Does It Steal Your Crypto?
partialText: Trojans are malicious software hidden inside apps or files that seem legitimate. Once inside your device, it may stay quiet for a while, without triggering any alarms. It can steal credentials or personal data, watch everything you type, modify your files, or turn your device into a zombie for their malicious network (botnet).

title: Growth Hacking Is Dead. Trust Is the New Growth Engine.
partialText: Growth hacking helped startups scale fast, but it rarely creates lasting companies. In today’s noisy digital landscape, trust is the real growth engine. Startups that focus on credibility, product experience, and community build stronger retention, lower CAC, and sustainable growth that compounds over time.

title: Why I Built Native Desktop Clients for Cloudflare D1, R2, KV, and Images
partialText: Cloudflare's dashboard and CLI leave gaps for day-to-day development work. I built four free native desktop apps (C++/Qt6) to fill them; a SQL editor for D1, an object browser for R2, a KV inspector, and a batch upload/variant preview tool for Images. Cross-platform, no Electron, credentials encrypted locally and never leave your machine.

title: The Silicon Renaissance: Gold Rush for Hardware Engineers in the AI Era
partialText: Software scales, but hardware is the new bottleneck. As Big Tech pivots from silicon consumers to chip creators, a new "Silicon Renaissance" has emerged.

title: Most Teams Know Bad On-Call. Few Can Define Good On-Call.
partialText: Healthy on-call isn’t just about reducing incidents. It’s about making sure load is fair, ownership is clear, runbooks are useful, heroics are rare, and engineers can recover after a rough shift. If a rotation depends on the same people absorbing the hardest pages and the human cost stays invisible, it isn’t healthy, even if the system stays up.

title: The Analogy Between Programming and the Architecture of the Universe
partialText: The Universe, perhaps, is not just "similar" to a computer. It fundamentally utilizes the same engineering principle on which the entire IT industry rests. If we try to deconstruct the physical world into layers, we will see practically perfect symmetry.

title: Your Infrastructure Will Fail. Here's How to Make It Fix Itself.
partialText: Modern AI infrastructure is too complex for manual incident response. Self-healing systems combine telemetry pipelines, anomaly detection, and automated remediation to detect failures early and repair them before users are impacted.

title: Mastering Database Functions: A Beginner's Guide to Simplifying Backend Code
partialText: A database function is a block of reusable code that lives inside your database. Think of it like a regular function in any programming language, except it runs inside the database engine. In Postgres, you write functions using a language called PL/pgSQL.

title: The Death of "Dumb Money": Why Stablecoins Are Finally Getting Smart
partialText: Stablecoins are evolving from simple value transfers to programmable assets with built-in compliance. New regulations (GENIUS Act, MiCA) treat them as digital money, not a separate asset class. Tokenized bank deposits from players like JPMorgan blur the line further. The result: settlement infrastructure that carries context, enforces rules across jurisdictions, and opens doors for automated treasury, conditional payments, and machine-to-machine transactions.

title: The Problem With How the Tech Industry Talks About 'Best Practices'
partialText: "Best practices" have stopped being tools and started being shields. Engineers cite them to avoid thinking, not to guide it. This is a problem for code quality, for junior devs, and for how we build software culture. Context always matters more than consensus.
